transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-24 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Opal CTO), Maya Thompson (Lead ML Eng), Derek Cho (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hi everyone—thanks for joining, I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE on this account. Miguel is our SE, Jordan might pop in for the infra bit. Can you do quick intros from Opal?
[00:15] Raj Patel: Yeah hi, Raj here, CTO at Opal. We build B2B analytics pipelines and starting to add generative features in our product. Maya?
[00:21] Maya Thompson: Maya, I lead ML engineering, mostly responsible for inference stack, latencies, cost.
[00:24] Derek Cho: Derek, platform engineering, we own infra, networking, security.
[00:28] Miguel Alvarez: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: integration patterns (SDKs, LL frameworks like LangChain / LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy model, rate limits and quotas, observability hooks, and next steps. Sound good?

[01:05] Raj Patel: Yep. High level context: we plan to ship a chat summarization feature and a semantic search index for enterprise customers. Two big concerns: P95 latency under 600ms for chat on short prompts, and data residency / auditability for some customers. Cost is also a factor — we have many daily queries.

[01:40] Miguel Alvarez: Understood. A couple clarifying q's: what's current stack for models — do you host models yourselves or using managed APIs?
[01:47] Maya Thompson: We currently use a mix. We started prototyping with OpenAI for prototyping but want to move to something more predictable cost and where we can control data. We also run some on-prem models for sensitive customers but it's been brittle.

[02:10] Sophie Chen: Okay, that fits the usual Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private conversation. For integration, do you prefer SDKs or self-hosted LangChain-style connectors?
[02:18] Raj Patel: We prefer programmatic SDKs, but our ML team heavily uses LangChain and LlamaIndex — so examples there would help.

[02:35] Miguel Alvarez: Great — Redwood has first-class REST + SDKs (Python/Node) and we provide adapters/examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Typical pattern we see: devs use the Redwood SDK for authentication and streaming, and a lightweight gateway/proxy sits in front of Redwood for routing, rate limiting and caching.

[03:00] [03:00] Miguel Alvarez: For LangChain we have connector snippets that show using Redwood as the LLM endpoint via the LLM wrapper - small code sample: 'from redwood import RedwoodLLM' then you can plug into chains. With LlamaIndex we show how to use Redwood to store embeddings and run rerank.

[03:28] Maya Thompson: Is that the official Redwood SDK or community examples?
[03:33] Miguel Alvarez: It's official SDK plus community examples. We maintain the SDK and the integration recipes in our repo. Some of the examples are community contributed but vetted by our team.

[04:00] Raj Patel: What about latency? If we go Hosted vs Dedicated, how much control do we have over latency SLOs? Our P95 600ms target is strict.

[04:12] Miguel Alvarez: Hosted gives you low friction and good latency for typical requests; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. For chat with short contexts, Dedicated with half-precision quantized models often meets sub-600ms P95 depending on model choice. We can share benchmarks. Note some variance due to sequence length and batching.

[04:45] Derek Cho: Can Dedicated be in our VPC?
[04:48] Sophie Chen: Redwood Dedicated can be set up with network peering or private connectivity; for fully private we offer Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane or on-prem options. Derek, that might be relevant for your compliance customers.

[05:05] Maya Thompson: On quotas/rate limits — we want to throttle per-customer usage and have burst capacity for spikes. Can we enforce per-API-key quotas and per-route limits?

[05:14] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, Redwood supports per-key quotas, rate limits at the route/model level, and token-based billing. You can set policies to tier customers and apply autoscaling or fallbacks to cheaper variants when limits are hit.

[05:36] Raj Patel: How would a gateway/proxy fit — is that required?

[05:40] Miguel Alvarez: Not required, but recommended for enterprise setups. Typical gateway does auth, per-tenant routing, caching of prefix responses, and local rate limiting. It also lets you do request shaping before sending to Redwood. We can provide an example proxy config (Nginx/envoy + small auth layer) and a sample Helm chart if you run Kubernetes.

[06:05] Derek Cho: Would that proxy be open-source or do we build it?

[06:08] Miguel Alvarez: We provide reference proxy configs and an open-source starter; most customers adapt it. We'll share the repo link.

[06:30] [06:30] Maya Thompson: Observability is huge — we need tracing, per-request logs, latency breakdowns, token-level cost attribution, and ability to hook to our datadog / prometheus.

[06:42] Miguel Alvarez: Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token cost and latency breakdowns. There's tracing hooks and a telemetry API. For customers on Dedicated/Private, we can send metrics to your Prometheus or push events to your datadog using a connector. We also expose structured logs and optional request-level metadata for audit trails.

[07:10] Raj Patel: Is the request metadata PII-safe? We need to ensure we don't log the customer text for some tenants.

[07:16] Sophie Chen: You can configure redaction rules and disable logging of request bodies for sensitive tenants. For Private deployments you control logs entirely.

[07:35] Derek Cho: On encryption— KMS support? HSM? We have strict key management policies.

[07:41] Miguel Alvarez: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers and offer HSM-backed key management for Private installs. We'll share the security whitepaper.

[08:05] Raj Patel: Ok good. A technical question: how do embeddings work with LangChain/LlamaIndex integration? Do we host vector DB or do you integrate with customers' vector DB?

[08:16] Miguel Alvarez: Redwood provides embeddings endpoints — you can send text and get vectors. We don't offer managed vector DB as part of Redwood but provide connectors/examples for common vector stores (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, also self-hosted options). For LlamaIndex we show how to plug Redwood embeddings into the index builder.

[08:40] Maya Thompson: Any notes on tokenization differences across models — we saw some variance between open models when calculating token cost.

[08:47] Miguel Alvarez: Yes tokenization differs. We surface token usage per request so you can profile costs. We also recommend model recommendations & quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize to reduce per-token cost for production workloads.

[09:10] Raj Patel: For the demo/proof-of-concept we want to: 1) wire up LangChain with Redwood as LLM + embeddings, 2) run a 48-hour benchmark with our test corpus, and 3) evaluate Dedicated baseline vs Hosted. Is that feasible?

[09:25] Miguel Alvarez: Absolutely. Typical POC: we provide SDK examples and a small helm chart for proxy; you run benchmark harness and we run concurrent bench on our side. For Dedicated we can offer a short reserved environment for POC — need to coordinate capacity.

[09:40] Sophie Chen: Timeline question: what's your target for rolling this to customers?

[09:44] Raj Patel: We'd like to GA in Q4, so POC and security review need to happen in next 6-8 weeks.

[09:52] Sophie Chen: That timeline is reasonable. Next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs, Miguel will send LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and proxy config, and Derek will share traffic profiles.

[10:10] [10:10] Maya Thompson: One more question about fallback policies — we sometimes want to degrade gracefully to smaller models when high traffic. Is that automatic?

[10:18] Miguel Alvarez: We have routing policies that can fallback to compatible model variants (e.g., 13B quantized) when capacity constrained or to meet cost targets. You can set those per-route and configure A/B or canary rollouts.

[10:38] Raj Patel: Security review: is there SOC2? ISO?

[10:42] Sophie Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 documentation; we'll attach the attestation and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.

[11:00] Derek Cho: For Private deployment, how heavy is the ops burden? We need to understand upgrades, telemetry, and support SLAs.

[11:10] Miguel Alvarez: Private comes with an ops runbook. We support managed upgrades and provide observability connectors; support SLA levels are part of enterprise terms. We can scope that with our customer success team after POC.

[11:30] Maya Thompson: Are there any gotchas with LangChain — for example streaming or function calling compatibility?

[11:36] Miguel Alvarez: We support streaming and structured outputs; function calling patterns can be implemented with our SDKs. There are small differences in event shapes — our LangChain recipe covers streaming handlers.

[12:00] Raj Patel: For onboarding, what's the dev experience like — keys, staging, rate limits?

[12:06] Sophie Chen: Dev experience: you create per-team API keys, set quotas, and use our SDK to switch environments (staging/production). We also give usage analytics per-key.

[12:25] [12:25] Raj Patel: Cost question — if we do heavy embedding workloads, are we billed by token or per-embedding?

[12:30] Miguel Alvarez: Embeddings are billed per-embedding (unit pricing) and generative tokens are billed per-token. We'll include a cost model in the pricing doc so you can estimate.

[13:00] Maya Thompson: Any notes about throttling and queueing? We want to avoid long tail queues for interactive flows.

[13:08] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, you can prioritize low-latency routes and enable smart batching for background jobs. For interactive chat we recommend small batch sizes and dedicated capacity.

[13:35] Raj Patel: What about model version pinning and rollbacks in case of regressions?

[13:40] Miguel Alvarez: You can pin model versions per-route and do canary/A-B rollouts using the Console. We also support quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals.

[14:05] [14:05] Sophie Chen: Any internal stakeholder we should loop in for security/compliance?

[14:10] Raj Patel: I'll loop in our Head of Security, Priya, after we review the docs. She'll likely want the SOC2 and KMS/HSM details.

[14:30] Derek Cho: About observability hooks — can we get per-token cost breakdowns pushed to our billing pipeline?

[14:36] Miguel Alvarez: We have an exportable usage API and webhooks; you can ingest token-level metrics into your billing pipeline.

[15:00] Maya Thompson: Would you be able to share a short sample that shows using Redwood with LangChain for a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flow?

[15:06] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, that's exactly the example we'll share: LangChain -> Redwood LLM wrapper + Redwood embeddings -> vector store connector -> retriever -> chain. We'll include code.

[15:28] [15:28] Raj Patel: Any concerns around model fingerprinting or determinism — we need reproducible outputs for regulatory reasons for some tenants.

[15:35] Miguel Alvarez: Determinism depends on model; you can set temperature to 0 and pin model versions. For strict reproducibility we recommend specific model variants and capture seed+metadata in audits. Private gives more control.

[16:00] Sophie Chen: Let's recap real quick and make sure we have alignment on next steps.

[16:06] Sophie Chen: Action items: I will send pricing and security docs; Miguel will send LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and proxy config; Derek will provide traffic profiles. We'll try to schedule a 90-minute technical deep dive next week focused on bench setup and Dedicated options. Any additions?

[16:30] Raj Patel: That covers it. One ask: can you include a sample SLO configuration we can share internally?

[16:36] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, we'll include example SLOs and dashboard templates.

[16:50] [16:50] Maya Thompson: Thanks everyone.

[16:52] Sophie Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the links and docs.

[16:55] Raj Patel: Bye.

Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache in one snippet depending on auto-transcribe). Links referenced: security whitepaper (link posted in follow-up), LangChain recipe repo (link to be shared), proxy starter repo (link to be shared).
